judge: Claude Code subagent, Claude Opus 5.5, fresh

items.label: A
items.critique: Directional repetition matches Westwood's guard style, but the opening 'shipment will be delayed' reason and the near-copy of another guard's line suggest it was modelled on one.

items.label: B
items.critique: The mocking jailer, the 'or a two!' slip, and the anticlimactic 'drinking binge again... Have a nice day' are Westwood's deadpan humour.

items.label: C
items.critique: Very flat and generic ('This is the home of', 'a great deed for our village'); could be a minor Westwood guard, but it gives the player nothing specific and reads like filler built to the template.

items.label: D
items.critique: The long, florid gate speech ('fairest of all villages in the land of Nox... open warm arms of aid') is a signature Westwood welcome, with a clumsy grandness no imitation bothers with.

items.label: E
items.critique: A tidy escalation (warning, then 'Last warning') and a neat line about the cells; well-shaped but generic, with no plot hook or Nox colour.

items.label: F
items.critique: Plausible gatekeeping, but 'meant for your own good... perils for the common man' is a little composed, and the three lines resolve neatly like a designed state machine.

items.label: G
items.critique: Hostility to a class ('blast you to oblivion') is Nox-like, but the checkpoint framing and the bare 'Sorry, the [Place] are closed' could be imitation; a guess.

items.label: H
items.critique: Plot-alarm exposition with Westwood's typographic slip ('look out' as two words) and the melodramatic 'curse of the necromancer come to haunt Nox again!'.

items.label: I
items.critique: The urgent mine-crisis greeting, the Foreman waiting outside, and 'Your valor knows no peer' are classic Westwood quest-hub guard lines.

items.label: J
items.critique: The three lines don't quite cohere (forbidden to pass, then go back west, then good luck in the mines, boy), which is the patchwork of Westwood's shared guard scripts.

tells: Westwood's guards serve the plot: they point at the current objective, raise alarms about the villain, or deliver a long civic welcome; generated guards tend toward generic gatekeeping with no specific hook.
Westwood's lines include small slips and odd humour (typos, 'a week, or a two', anticlimactic jokes); the new texts are clean and evenly paced.
Generated sets form a neat escalating arc (welcome, warning, last warning); Westwood's three lines are often stitched from different moments and don't flow.
Florid over-long speeches and exclamatory melodrama are a Westwood marker; the new writing is more restrained and uniform in length.
